entry.title: Speaking activation: verb-government gym + productive-vocabulary drill
entry.content:
Speaking activation: verb-government gym + productive-vocabulary drill

New silent, phone-first mode (app/activate.py) for turning passive vocabulary
active — the biggest gap between the learner's reading (B2+/C1−) and speaking
(A2/B1). One mode, two tracks:

- verb: a high-frequency verb + its GOVERNMENT (which case/preposition each
  argument takes). Curriculum: app/data/activate/verbs.json.gz — the 220 most
  common verbs, each with 1–3 argument patterns + example + the trap an English
  speaker falls into (built by build_activate_verbs.py). The learner's stated #1
  weakness.
- word: a common content word, introduced newest-frequent-first from the freq
  list.

Loop: app names a target + a concrete personalised thought to express; learner
forms the Russian in their head (reveal + self-grade) or types it (focused LLM
check — is the government right? one more fix, nothing else). SM-2-lite spacing;
prompt angle varies each time an item recurs. `mix` setting weights verbs/words
(default 0.65, heavy verbs early); `level` = gentle/standard/stretch.

/activate/{next,items/{id}/grade,stats,settings}. Active-word count on the Level
tab next to passive known_words, tracked daily (proficiency_snapshots.active_words).
See LEARNING.md. Frames (track 3) still to come.

Flow reading: listen (local TTS, background playback)

entry.content:
Card fronts show the stress; card backs show where the stress moves

- Word-mode study fronts now render the accented headword (audit_card fills
  dict_accented + upgrades front_word from the bundled stress dictionary), so
  you see the stress while learning the card, not after.
- accent.paradigm(): the key inflected forms of a noun/verb, shown on the card
  back ONLY when the stress actually moves (голова́ · го́ловы · го́лову …;
  пишу́ · пи́шет …). Fixed-stress words show nothing. Cached.
- accLine() renders the "stress moves:" block; _stress_for() wires it into the

entry.title: SRS: card integrity audit + repair, and don't re-surface cards review…
entry.content:
SRS: card integrity audit + repair, and don't re-surface cards reviewed today

- srs.audit_card(): structural check + in-place repair of a card that drifted —
  front_word that became the whole sentence, phrase/word mismatch, stray stress
  in the target, stale normalized_text, missing dictionary stress form. Content
  problems (target not in the sentence, no translation) are flagged for the LLM
  recheck. Runs in the background on every card create/edit (_audit_card_async),
  daily (_maybe_card_audit), and on demand (POST /srs/cards/audit).
- Daily-batch queue now excludes cards already reviewed today — a graduated card
  you've done can't come back the same day regardless of a sub-day `due`. Fixes
  "the cards that got added were the same ones I reviewed yesterday".
- Study front is derived from the card's own fields, so a stale front_html can't
  show a sentence when the setting says word. setCardFront reloads the queue.

entry.title: Anna Karenina readiness metric, religion domain, richer fiction style…
entry.content:
Anna Karenina readiness metric, religion domain, richer fiction style, reading sources on the word page

- app/books.py + build_book_vocab.py: bundled lemma-frequency profile of the full
  Anna Karenina (proper nouns / lemmatiser noise filtered). proficiency.book_readiness()
  turns it + what the learner knows into a token-coverage %, a difficulty read
  (Hu & Nation thresholds), and the frequent unknowns to target. Tracked daily
  (proficiency_snapshots.ak_coverage), shown on the Level tab with a sparkline and
  a "words that would help most" card-maker. reading_flow feeds the gaps into the
  fiction generator. GET /reading/books/{book} (+ /cards).
- New "Religion & philosophy" reading domain (Hindu/Buddhist thought, world
  religions) — essay register, grounded in real figures/texts.
- Fiction style now names the vocabulary of appearance, rooms, materials,
  colours, plants, smells, textures and nature — the stuff you only meet in
  novels.
- word_occurrences() indexes flow-reading chunks, so a word carded from the
  reading mode shows its context on the word page (was: "not seen anywhere").
- studyUndo: time-debounce + finally re-enables the button — one card per tap.
  tests/study_undo.test.mjs locks it.

entry.title: Flow reading: fixed-length pieces with a planned arc, plus sequels
entry.content:
Flow reading: fixed-length pieces with a planned arc, plus sequels

Each piece is now PARTS (5) parts with a real beginning/middle/end instead of
circling a theme forever. reading_flow_plan() draws a title + hook + per-part
beats first (a story arc, or an article's spine); each part is written to its
beat and the final part resolves. When it ends the reader gets an end card with
a "continue — a sequel, with a twist" button that spawns a linked session
(parent_id) whose plan opens on a reversal. Library shows N/5 progress and marks
sequels.

entry.title: Card format v2 groundwork: one clean primary meaning + concise altern…
entry.content:
Card format v2 groundwork: one clean primary meaning + concise alternatives

Not yet applied in bulk — this is the plumbing to prototype the new format on one
card and iterate.

- srs_cards.alt_meanings (other senses / idioms, small text on the back) +
  sentence_full (original long context, kept when `sentence` is trimmed to the
  clause with the word).
- llm.card_meaning(word, dict_form, sentence, current) -> {primary,
  primary_is_contextual, alt, context}: one cleanest general meaning as `primary`
  (contextual sense only when the usage is marked/idiomatic, and then `alt` leads
  with the general meaning); `context` is a substring-faithful trim to ~14 words.
- _study_card_view returns alt_meanings + a `reformatted` flag. studyReveal shows
  `.a-alt` under the big translation, and for reformatted cards shows ONLY the
  trimmed clause (no before/after context lines).
- Prototyped on card 413 (злоба): "malice / spite" → primary "malice" + alt;
  633-char paragraph → one clause; front стress fixed зло́ба.

entry.title: Fix /srs/queue 500 on a naive last_review timestamp
entry.content:
Fix /srs/queue 500 on a naive last_review timestamp

srs._row_to_fsrs fed the raw DB string to fsrs.Card.from_dict; a naive datetime
(from a restored backup, rebuild_db.py, or a hand-edit) made fsrs do
offset-naive − offset-aware arithmetic → TypeError → the whole study queue 500s.
`srs._aware()` coerces due/last_review to UTC-aware ISO first.

Verified the full study flow (reveal / rate / again / undo) and reader
phrase-selection with no console errors.
